title: Postmortem: Attention optimization heuristic caused mid-load latency degradation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: On 2025-02-09 we observed a sustained increase in P95/P99 latency for hosted inference requests driving long-sequence attention patterns. Root cause tracing points to a new kernel routing heuristic (deployed in runtime-1.19) that preferred a lower-memory kernel variant which performs poorly on long-sequence attention, causing KV-cache churn and scheduler backpressure under medium concurrency. The incident caused degraded user experience for a subset of customers using sequence lengths >2048 and throughput between 8-24 rps per GPU.
timeline: 2025-02-09 03:12 UTC - Alerts triggered: P95 latency spike on model-rw-v2 for region-us-west-2 (observability rule: inference.latency.p95 > 250ms).
2025-02-09 03:18 UTC - Oncall paged (eng-runtime). Initial hypothesis: upstream load injection or model change. Verified no model changes.
2025-02-09 03:30 UTC - Investigation found correlated drop in KV cache hit rate and increased kernel switch frequency in runtime logs.
2025-02-09 03:45 UTC - Rollforward in staging introduced kernel-routing heuristic 1.19.1 at 2025-02-08 22:05 UTC; rollout to prod at 2025-02-09 01:10 UTC.
2025-02-09 04:05 UTC - Mitigation: rollback runtime-1.19.1 to runtime-1.18.9 for affected pools. Latency P95 began returning toward baseline within 6 minutes.
2025-02-09 05:00 UTC - Post-rollback monitoring: systems stabilized; incident declared resolved at 05:22 UTC.
impact_summary: Duration ~2 hours 10 minutes (degradation window), affected small subset of customers with long-sequence/medium-concurrency workloads. Observed P95 latency increase from baseline ~180ms to peak ~460ms; P99 spikes to ~1.2s. Estimated customer error budget burn: 9% for affected SLA group. No data loss or correctness regressions reported.
root_cause: A change to the kernel routing heuristic favored a lower-memory attention kernel that performs well for short sequences but has O(N^2) inner-loop overhead constants that cause disproportionate runtime on long sequences. The heuristic lacked a cost model that incorporated sequence-length vs. kernel constant factors and failed to consider recent scheduler changes that increased continuous batching window, which amplified the effect. The combination triggered frequent kernel switching and KV cache invalidation, producing scheduling stalls and increased tail latency.
immediate_mitigation: Rollback runtime-1.19.1 to previous release for affected server pools (completed). Added temporary circuit-breaker: if sequence_length > 1024 then force kernel variant A (previous default). Increased observability: new dashboard for kernel-switch-rate and KV-cache-hit-rate per model and pool. Throttled staging rollout until fix verified.
long_term_actions: Add explicit cost model to kernel routing that accounts for sequence-length, attention algorithmic constants, and observed microbenchmarks (owner: Marcus Patel, due: 2025-03-07).
Introduce an e2e regression test that simulates mixed-length traffic with real KV-cache patterns to catch scheduling-amplified regressions (owner: Leila Thompson, due: 2025-02-28).
Refactor scheduler to expose a kernel-affinity signal so routing heuristic can request kernel stickiness for long-sequence traces (owner: Priya Rao, due: 2025-03-21).
Ship canary gating: require kernel-routing heuristic to pass perf gate (P95 and KV-hit thresholds) in canary region for 24h before global rollout (owner: SRE team, due: 2025-02-24).
Document runbook update for attention-related regressions and add automated alerts for kernel-switch-rate anomalies (owner: Oncall team, due: 2025-02-20).

PM (Jamal Ortiz) suggested exposing the kernel-affinity as an advanced control in dedicated deployments. Security reviewed and flagged no issues. Next steps: prioritize cost-model implementation before next runtime rollout.
